hindi: कर्म से कोई उसे नहीं पाता, जिसने सदा बढ़ने वाले इन्द्र को, यज्ञों से मानो, सब से स्तुत, बलवान, अजेय और बल से निर्भीक इन्द्र को बढ़ाया है।
english: No one reaches by deed him who has made Indra ever-growing, as it were through sacrifices: Indra, praised by all, mighty, unassailed, bold through strength.
notes: The construction is uncertain: na may be the negative of line 1 or the particle 'like' in line 2 (read here as 'as it were'); the object of cakāra is taken as Indra (sadāvṛdham agreeing with indram). kiṣṭam is read kiḥ + tam (na kiḥ, 'no one'). ṛbhvasam 'skilful, mighty' is uncertain.

hindi: वह जो बिना बन्धन के भी, कन्धे की हड्डियों के कटने से पहले, सन्धि को जोड़ने वाला है; वह धनवान मघवन् टूटे हुए को फिर ठीक करने वाला है।
english: He who, even without bandage, before the piercing of the collar-bones, joins the joint, the bountiful one rich in wealth, who sets right again what is broken.
notes: Hard verse: jatrubhya ātṛdaḥ (collar-bones / ātṛd 'piercing, cutting') and abhiśriṣaḥ (binding, bandage) are rendered literally; the sense of the phrase is uncertain. Read as a description of Indra (maghavā). Only the literal meaning is given, no medical interpretation.

words.gloss: and (ā … ā 'a thousand and a hundred')

hindi: हे इन्द्र, सोम पीने के लिए सोने के रथ में जुते हुए, प्रार्थना से जोड़े गए, लम्बे केशों वाले सैकड़ों-हजारों घोड़े तुम्हें यहाँ लाएँ।
english: May the long-maned bay horses, a thousand and a hundred, yoked to the golden chariot and harnessed by prayer, bring you here, O Indra, to drink the Soma.
notes: yuktā is read as yuktāḥ (Vedic nominative plural form). 'a thousand and a hundred' is the literal sense of sahasram ā śatam (a large number).

hindi: हे इन्द्र, आनन्द देने वाले, मोर के पंखों जैसे रोमों वाले घोड़ों के साथ आओ। कोई भी तुम्हें न रोके, जैसे जाल वाले (पक्षी को) रोकते हैं; उन्हें मरुभूमि की तरह पार कर जाओ।
english: Come, O Indra, with exhilarating bay horses with peacock-feather hair. Let none hold you back, as fowlers [hold a bird]; go beyond them as over a desert.

text_flags.why: possible: the Rigveda has 'ni yaman vim na pāśinaḥ' (as fowlers a bird); the Sāmaveda's 'yemur inna' may be a chant variant of this, so the word 'in' is uncertain

notes: 'yemur inna' is a Sāmaveda variant of the Rigveda 'yaman vim na'; the translation follows the RV sense ('as fowlers [hold] a bird'), the bird being understood. In words, inna is split in + na, with 'in' uncertain.

hindi: हे सबसे बलवान देव, तुम ही मनुष्य को आशीर्वाद देते हो। हे मघवन्, तुमसे अन्य कोई दयालु नहीं है; हे इन्द्र, मैं तुमसे यह वचन कहता हूँ।
english: You indeed, O god, most mighty, speak well of the mortal. There is no one other than you, O bountiful one, who is gracious; O Indra, I speak this word to you.

text_flags.why: possible: ar for ṛ in a chant-orthography spelling; the word is mṛḍitā 'gracious one'

notes: pra śaṃsiṣaḥ is taken as 'praise, speak well of, favour'; the exact nuance is uncertain. 'marḍitā' read as mṛḍitā (agent noun of √mṛḍ, to be gracious).

hindi: हे इन्द्र, तुम यशस्वी, बलवान और बल के स्वामी हो। तुम अकेले ही बहुत से शत्रुओं को बिना रोक-टोक मारते हो; किसी से प्रेरित नहीं, प्रजाओं के धारक।
english: You, O Indra, are glorious, mighty, lord of strength. You alone slay the foes irresistibly, much unimpelled by any, supporter of the peoples.
notes: ṛjīṣin (rendered 'mighty one') and apratīni (taken as an adverb 'irresistibly'; possibly n. acc. pl. 'unopposed') are uncertain. puru anuttaḥ: 'purv anuttaḥ' by sandhi; read 'much / often, unimpelled'.

words.gloss: for the worship of the gods

hindi: देवों की उपासना के लिए इन्द्र को ही (बुलाते हैं), यज्ञ के चलते समय इन्द्र को; हम उत्सुक उपासक युद्ध में इन्द्र को बुलाते हैं, धन की प्राप्ति के लिए इन्द्र को।
english: We call Indra indeed for the worship of the gods; Indra, when the sacrifice proceeds; we, the eager ones, call Indra in battle; Indra for the winning of wealth.

text_flags.why: possible: the 1 pl. middle ending is -mahe; the final -a may be a chant variant or a typing slip

notes: 'we call' is supplied from havāmahe for the first three Indra phrases. vaninaḥ (here 'eager ones, suppliants') is uncertain.

hindi: हे बहुधन, मेरी ये वाणियाँ तुम्हें बढ़ाएँ। निर्मल रंग वाले, शुद्ध, ज्ञानी (स्तोताओं) ने स्तोत्रों से तुम्हारी स्तुति की है।
english: May these songs of mine strengthen you, O rich in wealth. The pure, bright-coloured, inspired ones have praised [you] with their hymns.
notes: The object of abhi anūṣata (you) is understood. pāvakavarṇāḥ may describe the singers or the songs; taken as the singers.

hindi: वे अत्यन्त मधुर वाणियाँ और स्तोत्र ऊपर उठते हैं; सदा विजयी, धन जीतने वाले, अक्षय सहायता वाले, पुरस्कार चाहने वाले रथों की तरह।
english: Those sweetest songs and hymns rise up, ever-victorious, winning wealth, of unfailing help, like chariots striving for the prize.

text_flags.why: possible: visarga missing before the following s of stomāsa; read as giraḥ

notes: The agreement of line 2 (nominative plural adjectives) with stomāsaḥ/giraḥ is taken as 'the hymns, like chariots'; the sense of the simile is literal.

hindi: जैसे प्यासा जंगली बैल जल से बने स्थान पर जाता है, वैसे ही हमारे निकट आने और बढ़ने पर शीघ्र आओ; कण्वों के बीच साथ मिलकर अच्छी तरह पियो।
english: As a thirsty wild bull goes to the place made by the waters [the barren ground], so come quickly to us in our approach and advance; drink well together among the Kaṇvas.
notes: apā kṛtam, averiṇam, āpitve and prapitve are uncertain; rendered literally. averiṇam read as ava-iriṇam or a variant of iriṇa 'barren ground, salt-lick'; no firm reading. kaṇveṣu 'among the Kaṇvas' (the sage family) is a proper name.

hindi: हे शक्तियों के स्वामी इन्द्र, सब सहायताओं से भली-भाँति सहायता करो; क्योंकि हे शूर, हम तुम्हारे पीछे चलते हैं, जो यशस्वी और धन पाने वाले हो, जैसे भग (भाग्यदाता) के पीछे।
english: Help us well, O lord of powers, Indra, with all your aids; for we follow you, O hero, the glorious finder of wealth, as one follows Bhaga.
notes: The 3 in śagdhyū3ṣu is the pluta mark (prolongation) on ū. The comparison 'bhagaṃ na' is taken as 'like Bhaga', Bhaga being the bestower of fortune.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, ज्योति पाने वाले तुमने असुरों से जो भोग लाए, (उनसे) हे मघवन्, इस स्तोता को बढ़ाओ और जिन्होंने तुममें कुश बिछाया है, उन्हें भी।
english: O Indra, winner of the light of heaven, [with] the enjoyments that you brought from the Asuras, make this singer grow, O bountiful one, and those who have strewn the sacred grass for you.
notes: yā is read as yāḥ (acc. pl. f. relative agreeing with bhujaḥ). asya vardhaya: 'make grow' with asya ('of this') is uncertain; read as 'this (singer)'. svarvān follows the glossary: svar = light of heaven.

hindi: मित्र और अर्यमा के लिए संगति योग्य (स्तोत्र) गाओ, हे सत्यधन वाले; रक्षक वरुण के लिए मनभावन वचन और स्तुति-गान राजाओं में गाओ।
english: Sing forth to Mitra and to Aryaman a song fit for fellowship, O rich in truth; sing to Varuṇa the protector a pleasing word, a song of praise, among the kings.
notes: ṛtāvaso is read as a vocative 'O rich in truth' (uncertain; addressee unclear). varūthye3 is taken as a locative agreeing with varuṇe with a pluta mark (e3); the Rigveda has varūthyam (acc.) agreeing with vacaḥ, so the Sāmaveda form is a variant and the reading is uncertain. The addressed 'kings' are Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, पहले पीने के लिए मनुष्य स्तोत्रों से तुम्हारी ओर (आते हैं)। संगठित ऋभुओं ने मिलकर गाया; रुद्र प्राचीन (तुम) की स्तुति करते हैं।
english: Men [come] to you with hymns, O Indra, for the first drinking. The united Ṛbhus sang together; the Rudras praise you, the ancient one.
notes: abhi is taken with an understood verb ('approach / praise'). Whether pūrvyam is Indra (taken here) or a thing praised is not certain.

hindi: हे मरुतो, महान इन्द्र के लिए प्रार्थना-स्तोत्र उठाओ। वृत्रहन्ता, सैकड़ों शक्तियों वाला (इन्द्र) सौ गाँठों वाले वज्र से वृत्र को मारता है।
english: O Maruts, raise a prayer to great Indra. The slayer of Vṛtra, of a hundred powers, slays Vṛtra with the hundred-jointed thunderbolt.
notes: vaḥ is rendered 'for you' (dative of interest). Vṛtra is treated as a name.

hindi: हे मरुतो, वृत्र के सर्वश्रेष्ठ संहारक इन्द्र के लिए बृहत् (साम) गाओ, जिससे सत्य को बढ़ाने वालों ने ज्योति उत्पन्न की; देव के लिए दिव्य, जागरूक (गान)।
english: Sing the great chant (Bṛhat) to Indra, O Maruts, the best slayer of Vṛtra, by which those who strengthen truth brought forth light: a divine, wakeful [song] for the god.
notes: bṛhat may be the name of the chant (Bṛhat sāman) or simply 'great (song)'; devam jāgṛvi is taken as 'divine, wakeful (song)' for the god.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, जैसे पिता पुत्रों के लिए, वैसे हमारे लिए बुद्धि-कौशल लाओ। हे बहुतों से पुकारे गए, इस यात्रा में हमारी सहायता करो, कि हम जीवित रहते हुए प्रकाश पाएँ।
english: O Indra, bring us insight, as a father does for his sons. Help us, O much-invoked one, on this course, so that we may attain the light while living.
notes: śikṣā is the Vedic lengthened form of śikṣa; ṇo is naḥ.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हमें मत छोड़ो; हमारे साझे आनन्द-भोज में हमारे साथ रहो। तुम हमारी सहायता हो, तुम्हीं हमारे बन्धु हो; हे इन्द्र, हमें मत छोड़ो।
english: Do not forsake us, O Indra; be with us at the common feast. You are our help, you alone are our kinship; do not forsake us, O Indra.
notes: ūtī is read as 'help' (nominative; an instrumental 'by aid' is also possible). sadhamādye 'at the common feast' is a locative. bhavā is bhava with Vedic lengthening; vṛṇag is vṛṇak with voicing before bh.

hindi: हम, सोम निचोड़ने वाले और कुश बिछाने वाले, जल की तरह; हे वृत्रहन्, पवित्र छन्ने की धाराओं पर स्तोता तुम्हारे चारों ओर बैठते हैं।
english: We, indeed, having pressed the Soma and strewn the sacred grass for you, like waters; the singers sit around you, O slayer of Vṛtra, at the streams of the filter.
notes: 'like waters' (āpo na) is unclear in function (it may qualify the Soma streams or the worshippers); rendered literally.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, नहुष की प्रजाओं में जो बल है और जातियों में जो पौरुष है, अथवा पाँचों जनों का जो तेज है, वह सब हमारे लिए ले आओ, सब पुरुषार्थ पूरी तरह ले आओ।
english: Whatever strength and manly vigour, O Indra, [is] among the Nahuṣa peoples and the tribes, or whatever glory [belongs] to the five peoples, bring [it] here, altogether, all manly deeds.
notes: nāhuṣīṣu is read as 'among the Nahuṣa (peoples)'; the ā after it is taken with ā bhara in line 2 (separated prefix). 'for us' is not in the text.

hindi: सचमुच तुम बैल जैसे बलवान हो, बैल जैसे वेग वाले हमारे रक्षक। हे उग्र, तुम दूर में बलवान सुने जाते हो, और निकट में भी बलवान प्रसिद्ध हो।
english: Truly you are mighty as a bull, our helper of bull-like impulse. For, O fierce one, you are heard of as the bull in the far, and renowned as the bull in the near.
notes: vṛṣan 'bull' is rendered 'mighty as a bull'; vṛṣajūtiḥ 'of bull-like impulse' is a literal bahuvrīhi.

hindi: हे शक्र, तुम चाहे दूर हो या निकट, हे वृत्रहन्, वहाँ से भी, हे इन्द्र, सोम निचोड़ने वाला स्तुतियों के साथ और लम्बे केशों वाले (घोड़ों) के साथ तुम्हें यहाँ मनाता है।
english: Whether you are in the far, O mighty one, or in the near, O slayer of Vṛtra, from there the Soma-presser seeks to win you, O Indra, with songs and with the long-maned [horses].
notes: dyugat is uncertain (read as 'heaven-going / heavenly'); the grouping of gīrbhiḥ and keśibhiḥ with vivāsati is also uncertain. vivāsati (desiderative of √vas 'shine'?) is rendered 'seeks to win, propitiates' as an approximation.

hindi: तुम्हारे वीर, ज्ञानी (इन्द्र) के लिए सोमरस के मद में महान वाणी से गाओ; उस प्रसिद्ध, शक्तिशाली इन्द्र को नाम से, जैसे वचन (कहता है)।
english: Sing to your hero, the wise one, with a great song in the exhilaration of the juice; [sing] Indra by name, the renowned, the powerful, as the word [says].
notes: vaco yathā is unclear ('as the word says / according to the word'). 'to your hero' takes abhi with gāya; the addressee of gāya is the singer or the priests.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, कल्याण के लिए तिहरा शरण और तिहरा कवच दो; धनी यजमानों को और मुझे आश्रय दो; इनसे (शत्रु के) अस्त्र को दूर रखो।
english: O Indra, [grant] a threefold refuge, a triple shelter for welfare. Grant shelter to the bountiful patrons and to me, and keep the missile away from these.
notes: 'grant' in line 1 is supplied from yaccha. maghavadbhyaḥ 'bountiful ones' are the patrons.

hindi: सूर्य की शरण में आए हुओं की तरह तुम सब इन्द्र (के दानों) में भाग लो; बल से उत्पन्न हुआ (वह) धन देता है; हम अपने भाग की तरह (उसकी ओर) देखते हैं।
english: Like those who resort to the sun, all of you partake of Indra [his gifts]. [He,] born among beings with might, [gives] riches; we look to [him] as to our share.
notes: Hard verse; only a tentative literal sense is given. janimāni and jāto are uncertain, and the verbs of line 2 are supplied.

hindi: बिना देवता को माने हुआ दीर्घायु मनुष्य उस अन्न को नहीं पाता; वह जो चितकबरे घोड़ों के साथ चलने वाला है, जो अपना घोड़ा जोतता है, इन्द्र अपने दो हरे घोड़ों को जोतता है।
english: A godless mortal, even long-lived, has not obtained that refreshment; he who goes with dappled steeds, who yokes his steed, [that is] Indra; he yokes his two bay horses.

text_flags.why: possible: cit + yaḥ (ya before e); the long ā is unexplained
possible: 3 sg. middle ending -te, as in the second yuyojate of the same line

notes: Hard verse. etagvā cit yaḥ etaśaḥ yuyojate is read as 'he who goes with dappled steeds, who yokes his Etaśa'; the syntax connecting the two lines is uncertain. dīrghāyo is read as dīrghāyaḥ (stem uncertain).

words.gloss: O one equal to the hymn (?)

hindi: हमारे लिए सब युद्धों में पुकारने योग्य इन्द्र का सत्कार करो; हे वृत्रहन्, परम बल वाले, ऋचा के समान (योग्य), हमारी प्रार्थनाओं और सोम-सवनों के निकट आओ।
english: Attend on Indra, who is to be invoked in all battles, for us; [come] near our prayers and Soma-pressings, O slayer of Vṛtra, O one of supreme might, O equal to the hymn.
notes: Hard verse. bhūṣata (2 pl.) is taken as 'attend on, honour'; paramajyā and ṛcīṣama are uncertain (ṛcīṣama is an epithet of Indra, 'equal to the hymn / matching the verses'); 'come' in line 2 is supplied.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, सबसे निम्न धन तुम्हारा ही है; तुम बीच वाले का पोषण करते हो। तुम सब पर और सबसे ऊँचे पर पूरी तरह शासन करते हो; गौओं के विषय में कोई तुम्हें नहीं रोकता।
english: Yours indeed, O Indra, is the lowest wealth; you nourish the middle [one]. You rule altogether over all and over the highest; no one obstructs you in the matter of cattle.
notes: avamam vasu and madhyamam are read as 'lowest wealth' and 'the middle [wealth]'; vṛṇvate is taken as 'obstruct, hold back' (alternative 'choose').

hindi: तुम कहाँ जाते हो? कहाँ हो? तुम्हारा मन तो अनेक स्थानों में है। हे योद्धा, हलचल मचाने वाले, हे पुरन्दर, तुम दौड़ते हो; गायत्र गाने वालों ने गान किया है।
english: Where do you go? Where are you? For your mind is in many places. You hasten, O warrior, maker of tumult, O destroyer of forts; the Gāyatra singers have sung forth.
notes: alarṣi and khajakṛt are uncertain (khaja read as 'tumult, commotion'). gāyatrāḥ is taken as 'singers of Gāyatra verses'.

hindi: हम आज और कल यहाँ इस वज्रधारी को तृप्त करते आए हैं; उसके लिए आज सवन में निचोड़ा हुआ सोम लाओ और अब उस प्रसिद्ध का सत्कार करो।
english: Today and yesterday we have strengthened him here, the wielder of the thunderbolt; bring the pressed Soma to him today at the pressing, and now honour the renowned one.
notes: hyopīpemeha is read hyaḥ apīpema iha. bharā read as bhara (Vedic lengthening; 2 pl.). śrute is uncertain (dative/locative 'to the renowned one').

hindi: जो प्रजाओं का राजा है, रथों पर चलने वाला, अदम्य है, सब सेनाओं को पार करने वाला, जो सबसे श्रेष्ठ वृत्रहन्ता है, उसकी मैं स्तुति करता हूँ।
english: He who is king of the peoples, who goes in chariots, irresistible, the overcomer of all hosts, the foremost, who is the slayer of Vṛtra: I praise [him].
notes: jyeṣṭham (foremost) is taken as the object of gṛṇe with the relative clauses; 'him' is supplied.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, जिससे हम डरते हैं, उससे हमें अभय करो। हे मघवन्, सहायता करो; तुम्हारा वह (बल) हमारी रक्षा के लिए है; शत्रुओं को दूर मारो, आक्रमणकारियों को दूर मारो।
english: From whatever we fear, O Indra, make safety for us from that. O bountiful one, help; that [power] of yours is for our protection. Strike away the enemies, strike away the foes.
notes: tava tan na ūtaye is read as 'that [power/help] of yours is for our protection' (the noun is supplied).

hindi: हे घर के स्वामी, दृढ़ स्तम्भ, सोमपात्र जनों का सत्र; प्राचीन पुरों का भेदने वाला, बूँद के समान (वीर) इन्द्र, मुनियों का मित्र।
english: O lord of the dwelling, firm pillar, the session of the Soma-worthy ones; the drop (the bold one), breaker of the ancient forts, Indra, friend of the sages.
notes: Hard verse. dhruvā sthūṇām, satram and drapsaḥ are uncertain; the line seems to be a string of epithets of Indra with no verb. 'sthūṇā~' is read as sthūṇām (candrabindu before s).

hindi: सचमुच, हे सूर्य, तुम महान हो; सचमुच, हे आदित्य, तुम महान हो। तुम जो हो, तुम्हारी महिमा महान है, हे सबसे प्रशंसनीय; हे देव, तुम अपनी महिमा से महान हो।
english: Truly, O Sūrya, you are great; truly, O Āditya, you are great. Great is the greatness of you who are, O most admirable; by greatness, O god, you are great.
notes: baṇ- in baṇmahā~ is baṭ with nasal assimilation before m. mahaste sato is read mahaḥ te sataḥ.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, तुम्हारा जो मित्र है, वह घोड़ों, रथ, सुन्दर रूप और गायों वाला है; वह सदा पूर्ण बल-आयु से युक्त रहता है और चमकती (वस्तुओं) के साथ सभा में जाता है।
english: He who is your friend, O Indra, has horses, a chariot, a fair form and cattle; he is always accompanied by vigorous life, and goes to the assembly with shining [things].
notes: śvātrabhājā is uncertain (śvātra read as 'vigour, quickness'; the form agrees with vayasā). candraiḥ 'with shining (ornaments, gold)' is a tentative rendering.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, यदि तुम्हारे लिए सौ द्यौ और सौ भूमियाँ हों, तो भी, हे वज्रधारी, हज़ार सूर्य भी तुम्हारे बराबर नहीं हैं; उत्पन्न हुए दोनों लोक भी तुम्हें नहीं पा सके।
english: Even if there were a hundred heavens and a hundred earths for you, O Indra, a thousand suns would not match you, O wielder of the thunderbolt; nor have the two worlds, once born, reached you.
notes: anu with na is read as 'would not match / follow'; aṣṭa is read as 3 sg. aorist of √aś 'reach'. śata~ is śatam (candrabindu before s).

hindi: हे इन्द्र, चाहे पूर्व, पश्चिम, उत्तर या दक्षिण में मनुष्य तुम्हें पुकारें, तुम सब ओर बहुत स्थानों में मनुष्यों से प्रेरित हो; हे साहसी, तुम आनव में हो, तुर्वश में हो।
english: Whether you are invoked by men in the east, west, north or south, O Indra, you are everywhere, in many places, urged on by men; you are among the Ānavas, O bold one, among the Turvaśas.
notes: The four directions prāk/apāk/udak/nyak are read as east/west/north/south as is usual, with the literal sense 'forward/backward/upward/downward' also possible. simā is read sīm ā (uncertain). Ānava and Turvaśa are tribal names.

words.gloss: wealth, one whose wealth you are

hindi: हे इन्द्र, कौन मनुष्य उसपर आक्रमण करने का साहस करता है जिसके धन तुम हो? हे मघवन्, निर्णायक दिन में, श्रद्धा से वाजी (योद्धा) पुरस्कार पाना चाहता है।
english: O Indra, what mortal dares [attack] him whose wealth you are? For with faith in you, O bountiful one, on the decisive day the prize-seeker strives to win the prize.

text_flags.why: possible: the Rigveda has tvāvasum 'having you as wealth' plus ā; the printed split 'tvā vasavā' looks like a corruption

notes: The two tokens tvā, vasavā are read as tvā-vasum ā by comparison with the Rigveda, but this is a suggestion only. pārye divi is uncertain ('decisive day'); śraddhā hi te is taken as 'with faith in you'.

hindi: हे इन्द्र और अग्नि, यह बिना पैरों वाली पैरों वाली (सब) से पहले आ गई है; सिर को छोड़कर, जीभ से पुकारती, चलती हुई उसने तीस पग रखे।
english: O Indra and Agni, this footless one has come before the footed ones; leaving the head, crying with the tongue, moving, she has stepped thirty steps.
notes: A riddle verse; the subject is not named in the text (traditionally dawn, not stated here). pūrvā agāt is read as 'she has come first'.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, निकट आओ, नपी-तुली बुद्धि वाली सहायताओं के साथ; हे अत्यन्त कल्याणकारी, अत्यन्त कल्याणकारी सहायताओं के साथ आओ; हे अच्छे मित्र, अच्छे मित्रों के साथ आओ।
english: Come nearer, O Indra, with aids of measured wisdom; come, O most beneficent one, with most beneficent succours; come, O good friend, with good friends.
notes: The words śaṃ + tama and śaṃ + tamābhiḥ are printed apart but are the compounds śaṃtama 'most beneficent' (voc.) and śaṃtamābhiḥ. mitamedhābhiḥ 'of measured wisdom' is uncertain.

hindi: यहाँ से सहायता के साथ तुम्हारे लिए अजर, प्रेरक, किसी से अप्रेरित, तेज़, विजेता, प्रेरित करने वाले, श्रेष्ठ रथी, अपराजित, तुग्रिय में बढ़ने वाले (इन्द्र को बुलाओ)।
english: From here, with help, [call] for yourselves the ageless one, the impeller, the unimpelled, the swift, the victor, the urger, the best of charioteers, the unconquered one, who grows in the Tugrya [waters ?].
notes: GROUPING: the unit has no finite verb (a list of epithets in the accusative); the sentence probably continues from or into the neighbouring verses. tugriyāvṛdham is uncertain ('growing in the Tugrya / strengthening Tugra's [people]'); the verb 'call' is supplied.

hindi: तुम्हें हमसे दूर कहीं पुरोहित भी न रोक रखें; दूर से या यहाँ पास होकर हमारे साझे आनन्द-भोज में आओ और सुनो।
english: Let not even the priests keep you far from us. Come to our common feast, whether from afar or here, and, being near, listen.

text_flags.why: possible: the Rigveda reading is 'vāghataś canāre asmat'; the printed split 'ca nāre' looks like a mis-division of cana + āre

notes: The jussive mā … rīraman is rendered 'Let not … keep'. vāghataḥ is taken as 'priests / sacrificers'. The end of line 2 is read vā san upa śrudhi ('or being near, listen'); the printed śrudhi corresponds to śṛṇudhi.

words.gloss: to the wielder of the thunderbolt

hindi: सोमपायी वज्रधारी इन्द्र के लिए सोम निचोड़ो; उसकी कृपा के लिए पकाई हुई वस्तुएँ पकाओ; (यह) करो; उदार देने वाला ही उदार को सुख देता है।
english: Press Soma for Indra, the Soma-drinker, the wielder of the thunderbolt; cook the cooked offerings for his favour; do it. The generous one indeed [gives] happiness to the generous one.
notes: 'do it' (kṛṇudhvam it) is a literal rendering with an unstated object. pṛṇan it pṛṇate mayaḥ is taken as 'the generous giver [gives] happiness to the one who gives'; its application (Indra / the patron) is not stated in the text.

hindi: जो सर्वविजयी और सबको देखने वाला इन्द्र है, उसे हम पुकारते हैं। हे सहस्र उत्साह वाले, हे महान पौरुष वाले, हे सज्जनों के स्वामी, युद्धों में हमारी वृद्धि के लिए हो जाओ।
english: Him who is all-conquering and all-surveying, Indra, we call. O thousand-spirited one, O one of great manliness, O lord of the good, be in battles for our increase.
notes: sahasramanyo is read as 'of a thousand spirits / wraths'; manyu has both senses, so 'spirited' is a neutral rendering. bhavā is bhava with Vedic lengthening.

words.gloss: O you two rich in power

hindi: हे शक्ति के धनी दोनों (देवो), अपनी शक्तियों से दिन-रात हमारी सहायता करो। तुम दोनों का दान कभी न घटे; तुम्हारा दान हमसे कभी दूर न हो।
english: With your powers, O you two rich in power, favour us by day and by night. May your gift never fail; may your gift never be [taken] from us.

text_flags.why: possible: the verb is daśasya 'favour, grant'; di- looks like a slip for da-
the particle cana is printed as two tokens ca + na

notes: The particle cana ('ever', with mā/na 'never') is printed as two tokens ca + na in both places; the tokens ca and na are glossed as its two halves. In line 2 the token nāsmadrātiḥ is cana's second half + asmat rātiḥ. The addressees (dual) are not named in the text.

hindi: जब कभी कोई मनुष्य स्तोता उदार (देव) की स्तुति करे, तब वह प्रेरित वाणी से वरुण की भी वन्दना करे, जो भिन्न-भिन्न व्रतों वालों का धारक है।
english: Whenever a mortal singer praises the bountiful one, then let him praise Varuṇa with an inspired song, the upholder of those of various rites.
notes: The 'bountiful one' (mīḍhvas) is not named in the text. vipā and vivratānām are uncertain ('inspiration'; 'of those of various rites / ordinances').

hindi: सोम के मद के लिए (गायों के) दूध से मिश्रित (रस) पियो, इन्द्र के लिए, मेध्यातिथि के लिए; जो दोनों हरे घोड़ों के साथ मिला हुआ है, जो सुनहरा है, वह वज्रधारी इन्द्र सुनहरा है।
english: Drink — the cows [milk ?], the exhilaration of the juice — for Indra, for Medhyātithi; he who is joined with the two bay horses, who is golden, Indra the wielder of the thunderbolt, golden.

text_flags.why: possible: the sense of 'gā andhaso mada' is unclear; gā read as gāḥ (cows / milk); mada may stand for made 'in the exhilaration'

notes: Obscure verse. Line 1 is not translated with certainty: pāhi with gāḥ, andhasaḥ and madaḥ/made, and the dative indrāya medhyātithe (Medhyātithi is a sage's name) are given a tentative reading. Line 2 lists Indra's qualities (sammiślaḥ with the two bay horses; golden; thunderbolt-wielder).

hindi: इन्द्र हमारे इन दोनों वचनों को, इस वाणी को पास से सुने; वह बलवान मघवन् सोम पीने के लिए हमारी एकाग्र प्रार्थना से यहाँ आए।
english: May Indra hear both of ours, this word turned toward him; may the bountiful, most mighty one come with [our] concentrated prayer to drink the Soma.
notes: 'both' (ubhayam) is left general (both praise and request is the usual reading, not stated here). satrācyā dhiyā is rendered 'concentrated prayer'. na (naḥ) is taken as 'ours'.

hindi: हे पत्थर के धारी, बड़े मूल्य के लिए भी तुम्हें दूर नहीं दिया जाता; हज़ार के लिए नहीं, दस हज़ार के लिए नहीं, हे वज्री, सौ के लिए भी नहीं, हे सौ दान वाले।
english: O wielder of the stone, you are not given away even for a great price; not for a thousand, not for ten thousand, O wielder of the thunderbolt, nor for a hundred, O hundred-gifted one.

text_flags.why: possible: dative ayutāya (parallel to sahasrāya, śatāya); -e looks like a slip

notes: mahe ca na is read mahe cana ('not even for a great [price]'). The Rigveda has a different verb (deyām 'may I give'); the Sāmaveda text dīyase is passive ('you are given'). adrivaḥ follows the glossary rendering (wielder of the stone).

hindi: हे इन्द्र, तुम मेरे लिए पिता से बेहतर हो, और न देने वाले भाई से भी; और हे वसु, मेरी माता और तुम दोनों समान रूप से धन पाने और सफलता के लिए (मुझे) आश्रय देते हो।
english: O Indra, you are better for me than a father and than a brother who does not share; and my mother and you two shelter [me] equally, O good one, for the winning of goods and for bounty.
notes: Line 2 is uncertain: chadayathaḥ is a dual verb ('you two shelter/cover'), with subjects my mother and (implied) Indra; vasutvanāya and rādhase are rendered tentatively. abhuñjataḥ is read as 'not sharing / not providing' (a-√bhuj).
